stories.headline: Chase DeLauter and Jos頒am𹑺 lead the Guardians to a 7-3 win over the Rays in Game 1 of the ALCS
stories.summary: — The Cleveland Guardians used small ball, the longball and played solid all-around baseball to keep winning in the postseason.
stories.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- — The Cleveland Guardians used small ball, the longball and played solid all-around baseball to keep winning in the postseason.


Nathaniel Lowe snapped an eighth-inning tie with a two-run single after Chase DeLauter and Patrick Bailey homered off Drew Rasmussen, and the Guardians rallied past the Tampa Bay Rays 7-3 in Game 1 of the American League Championship Series on Monday night.


After losing the first two games at home to the Chicago White Sox in their AL Division Series, Cleveland has won four straight in the postseason for the first time since winning their first six playoff games in 2016 on the way to a World Series berth.


“It feels good to see some balls fall, to see some guys get on the barrel, to see some guys have some great at-bats, because the first two games of the White Sox series, we got beat. We did,” Lowe said. “We had to go get our backs against the wall and do something crazy, and this group did. It’s nice to feel some momentum coming here and to take Game 1.”


Jose Ram𹑺 had three hits and DeLauter was a triple shy of the cycle as the Guardians banged out 14 hits against a Tampa Bay staff that allowed just 12 in its entire Division Series against the New York Yankees.


Junior Caminero and Jonny DeLuca had RBI singles in the first and Cedric Mullins hit a solo homer for the Rays, who never trailed in their three-game sweep of the Yankees.


“It’s been a while since we lost, so I think that’s a good thing, and I know the guys will come back and respond tomorrow,” Tampa Bay manager Kevin Cash said.


Game 2 is Tuesday night at Tropicana Field. Rookie left-hander Parker Messick starts for Cleveland, and right-hander Freddy Peralta takes the mound for the Rays.


Five relievers combined for five innings of one-run, two-hit ball for the Guardians, who became only the 11th team to overcome an 0-2 deficit in a best-of-five playoff series with a victory over the White Sox on Saturday night.


Hunter Gaddis worked a scoreless seventh for the win. Cade Smith, who pitched in all five games against Chicago, tossed a perfect ninth.


“Obviously we came off an emotional series, had a quick turnaround. But these guys come ready to play every day. Couldn’t be more proud of them,” Cleveland manager Stephen Vogt said. “We got punched early. And our pitching staff, credit to them, for stopping it and keeping us in the game as long as they did. And the offense came alive.”


Rasmussen took a 2-0 lead into the sixth before DeLauter led off with an opposite-field homer to left-center. Bailey started the seventh with a towering shot to center that went a projected 436 feet, ending Rasmussen’s night.


Rasmussen carried a no-hitter into the eighth in Game 1 of the ALDS against the Yankees.


Ram𹑺 opened the eighth with an infield single off losing pitcher Tyler Wells, and DeLauter ripped a double to right. After Wells retired Jo Adell on a grounder to second, Ian Seymour entered. Lowe lined an 0-2 pitch up the middle to drive in two, giving Cleveland a 4-2 lead.


Lowe made his major league debut with Tampa Bay in 2019 and won a World Series with Texas in 2023.


“I love coming back here, I really do,” Lowe said. “It’s nice to see some familiar faces on the other side.”


Mullins connected off Erik Sabrowski for a solo shot in the bottom half.


Ram𹑺, whose two-run homer lifted Cleveland to a 2-0 win in Game 5 against Chicago, provided an insurance run with an RBI single in the ninth off Cole Sulser.


Ram𹑺 then helped the Guardians get two more by breaking for third with two outs and two strikes on Adell. Caminero ran to cover the bag and was out of position when Adell hit a sharp grounder toward third. The ball rolled into left field for a two-run double.


A crowd of 35,361 fans waved yellow rally towels and rang cowbells at the Trop as Tampa Bay made its third ALCS appearance in the franchise's 29-season history.


They were fired up when the 98-win Rays jumped ahead 2-0 in the first and Rasmussen battled to keep it there until the sixth.


Coming off that dominant performance against the Yankees, Rasmussen went six-plus tough innings. The two-time All-Star right-hander, who was four outs from a no-hitter in a 1-0 victory against New York, allowed a hit to the second batter he faced and eight total, striking out seven.


Guardians starter Foster Griffin gave up two runs and five hits in four innings.


Glove work
The Rays helped Rasmussen with outstanding defense.


Nick Fortes threw out Ram𹑺 trying to steal second in the first. Caminero made an excellent play to retire Adell on a hard bouncer to third. Caminero short-hopped the ball with his backhand and fired a strong throw to first.


The Guardians had a runner on first with one out in the third when second baseman Ben Williamson robbed DeLauter of a hit that prevented a first-and-third jam. Williamson, who wasn’t on the ALDS roster, made a diving grab on DeLauter’s sharp grounder, got up and threw him out.


Stranded runners
Rays slick-fielding shortstop Taylor Walls was 0 for 3 and left six runners on base. He struck out with the bases loaded to end the first, lined out with a runner on in the fourth and grounded out with runners on first and second to end the sixth.


Up next
Messick took the loss in Game 1 of the AL Division Series, allowing two runs over 4 1/3 innings. He threw 2 1/3 innings in relief during a Game 4 victory, giving up two runs. Messick had 11 strikeouts in the two appearances. He was 12-9 with a 2.56 ERA in the regular season.


Peralta allowed one run and three hits over 4 2/3 innings in Game 2 of the Division Series vs. the Yankees. He was 5-2 with a 3.25 ERA in 10 starts after joining Tampa Bay at the trade deadline. Peralta was 5-9 with a 4.99 ERA for the Mets this season.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Barcelona, Real Madrid scout Erling Haaland at Anfield
stories.summary: Barcelona and Real Madrid continue to keep tabs on Erling Haaland, while Chelsea growing confident of signing Bournemouth's Alex Scott. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Barcelona and Real Madrid were at Anfield on Sunday to watch Erling Haaland when Manchester City faced Liverpool. Meanwhile, Chelsea are growing confident they will be able to sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott in January.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Barcelona and Real Madrid scouts were at Anfield to scout Manchester City striker Erling Haaland as he opened the scoring in a 3-0 win over Liverpool, according to TEAMtalk. Both of the Spanish giants continue to monitor the possibility of a future move following the club's guilty verdict for hundreds of financial charges. The two clubs weren't just there to watch City players, though: Barça have also been monitoring the situation of defender Ronald Araújo, who is on loan at Liverpool, while Madrid have been checking on Liverpool midfielders Alexis Mac Allister and Florian Wirtz.

- Chelsea are increasingly confident that they will sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott during the January transfer window, according to TEAMtalk. The belief is that the 23-year-old would find it difficult to turn down a move to Stamford Bridge and the Blues are willing to meet the Cherries' demands, with any deal likely to reach around £100 million. Bournemouth turned down all interest in Scott during the summer, but the England international's contract expires in 2028 and he has so far resisted any calls for an extension.

- Borussia Dortmund have been interested in U.S. youth international and Philadelphia Union striker Malik Jakupovic for some time, reports Sky Germany. In the summer, the Bundesliga club submitted an offer for the 17-year-old that was worth €2m-€3m but was ultimately rejected. Contact continues to exist but there is major competition for Jakupovic with Chelsea, RB Salzburg and Stuttgart all looking at him while Eintracht Frankfurt also have in the past.

- The summer transfer window may be long gone, but Getafe aren't waiting until January to make their signings as they are looking at free agents Dani Carvajal and Dani Parejo, reports Marca. Former Real Madrid right-back Carvajal has already reached an agreement and the paperwork for the move has been submitted. Having secured the 34-year-old, they are now aiming for Parejo after the midfielder's Villarreal contract expired in the summer and they have already made contact. Even after that, they could continue to look at free agents.

- Chelsea will need at least £50 million to tempt Barcelona into letting midfielder Frenkie de Jong leave in the January transfer window, according to Football Insider. Chelsea are looking at the 29-year-old as they continue their efforts to replace Enzo Fernández after the Argentina international joined Manchester City in the summer. De Jong is out injured but the Dutch midfield is nearing a return to fitness, although that return could make a move more difficult for the Blues as Barça have been eagerly awaiting his return.

Other
- Arsenal are keeping an eye on Michael Olise's contract talks with Bayern Munich as they continue to look at wingers. (FootballTransfers)

- Arsenal are yet to make a decision about Max Dowman's future amid interest in a loan from Celtic and Rangers. (Football Insider)

- Several major clubs are interested in a January move for Palmeiras right back Agustin Giay, with Atletico Madrid, AC Milan and Napoli having previously made approaches. (Matteo Moretto)

- Brighton & Hove Albion see RB Salzburg midfielder Bartosz Mazurek as a leading option for January, but they face competition from Benfica and Porto. (TEAMtalk)

- Borussia Dortmund have the right to match any offer for Monaco striker Paris Brunner. (Patrick Berger)

- Napoli have started to show an interest in Union Berlin winger Livan Burcu, who is also attracting attention from other top European clubs. (Rudy Galetti)

- Borrusia Dortmund remain interested in Zaglebie Lubin attacking midfielder Marcel Rugela, but a summer move for the 19-year-old is more likely than one in January. (Patrick Berger)

- Lazio have their eyes on 18-year-old winger Filippo Toscano from Serie D side Reggina as they look to the future. (Nicolo Schira)

- Johan Bakayoko is a possible candidate to leave RB Leipzig in January despite only joining the Bundesliga club last year. (Philipp Hinze)

- AC Milan are working for a way to offload 23-year-old midfielder Warren Bondo in January. (Nicolo Schira)

stories.headline: Sean McVay says Rams to 'evaluate everything' about kicking unit after OT loss
stories.summary: After the Rams missed a field goal attempt and had another blocked in Monday night's 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills, coach Sean McVay said Los Angeles will "evaluate everything" about the kicking unit.
stories.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- After the Rams missed a field goal attempt and had another blocked in Monday night's 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills, coach Sean McVay said Los Angeles will "evaluate everything" about the kicking unit.

Rams kicker Harrison Mevis missed a 50-yard field goal attempt wide left in the first quarter and had a 48-yard kick blocked in overtime that would have been the winner.

"In the kicking game, especially with our PAT, field goal, not even close to good enough," McVay said after the loss. "It cost us the game tonight."

The Rams have had three blocked field goal attempts since the start of last season, tied for the most in the NFL, according to ESPN Research. The Rams have had 81 missed or blocked kicks under McVay (since 2017, including playoffs), which is third most in the league.

"I felt like I hit it good," Mevis said. "That's all I can tell you. I mean, I hit it good, gave it a chance. I'll have to look."

On the play before the blocked kick, the Rams faced a third-and-5 from the Buffalo 30. Rams running back Kyren Williams was stopped for no gain on the play. After the game, McVay said he wished he had a better play call on third down.

"I'm sick that we came up short, and I'll be regretting kicking that and not having a better call to be able to go for it on third down and go to fourth or whatever it was," McVay said. "And that's on me."

McVay said, "It's been a while since I've been this pissed after a game."

"We go out there and we give the opportunity for our special teams to kind of go out there and get a field goal," said Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua, who finished with 17 catches for 138 receiving yards and a touchdown. "We got to be able to execute, and if that's not what we wanted to do, we got to find a way to convert on the critical downs."

The Rams fell to 2-3 despite Matthew Stafford going 40-for-54 for 383 yards and three touchdowns. Los Angeles is in third place in the NFC West behind the 5-0 San Francisco 49ers and 3-2 Seattle Seahawks.

stories.headline: When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old, who has the potential to set a new record for the youngest Formula 1 champion this year, now leads Mercedes teammate Russell by 102 points in the standings with a maximum of 150 points still up for grabs.

The substantial lead means he could be crowned champion as early as Oct. 24 at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, but the maths around that calculation are slightly complicated by question marks over the final two races of the season. The grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi are currently scheduled to go ahead on Nov. 29 and Dec. 6, but escalations in the war between the United States and Iran have the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

F1 has put a contingency plan in place to hold a single round at Imola if Qatar and Abu Dhabi are cancelled, but doing so would cut the championship short by one round and mean only 125 points are available to any single driver before the end of the year. Such a scenario would change the maths around the championship fight, making it easier for Antonelli to be crowned champion in Austin.

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

- Max Verstappen takes back-to-back wins with dominant drive at Singapore GP

- Lewis Hamilton calls Singapore GP strategy 'painful lesson' after Ferrari apology

Alongside Russell and Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris are still mathematically in contention for this year's championship, although the incredibly slim hopes of Leclerc and Norris would be snuffed out entirely by the cancellation of the races in the Middle East.

What does Antonelli need to do to be crowned champion in Austin?
Assuming the final two races go ahead as planned, Antonelli's chances of clinching the title in Austin remain relatively slim. The Mercedes driver would need to win in Texas, with his teammate Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton finishing fifth or lower.

Such a scenario would put Antonelli 125 points ahead of Russell with 125 points remaining, but even if Antonelli failed to score another point and Russell won all the remaining rounds after Austin, Antonelli would still be crowned champion on countback of race victories (by that stage Antonelli would be on nine and Russell on three with five races remaining).

If the championship is shortened by the season ending in Imola rather than Abu Dhabi, Antonelli would only need to leave Austin with a lead of 100 points over his rivals.

Such a scenario would result in the following permutations:

If Antonelli wins in Austin he would be crowned champion regardless of where the others finish.
If Antonelli finishes second, he would be crowned champion if Russell doesn't win the race.
If Antonelli finishes third, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes off the podium.
If Antonelli finishes fourth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes behind him and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes fifth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fourth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes sixth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fifth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes seventh, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes sixth or lower and Hamilton does not finish in the top two.
If Antonelli finishes eighth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes seventh or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top two and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes ninth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes eighth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes tenth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli fails to score, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton finishes fifth or lower and Verstappen does not win the race.

What's the minimum Antonelli needs to do be crowned champion?
Another way to look at the championship is the minimum amount of points Antonelli needs to score over the remaining rounds to secure the title regardless of what other drivers achieve. Assuming Qatar and Abu Dhabi go ahead, he needs 49 points over the remaining rounds, which could be achieved with as little as five sixth place finishes and one fifth place finish over the rest of the season.

If only five races remain, Antonelli would need just 24 points to secure the title, which would be attainable with two seventh place finishes and three eighth place finishes at the remaining rounds.

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Tuesday, Oct. 13
Blues land gun Giant

Lachie Whitfield's move to Carlton is official, with the 32-year-old joining the Blues on a three-year deal. Whitfield has played 278 games, and joins Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, and Jake Stringer in departing the Giants.

Carlton receive picks 31 and 50 along with the veteran, with pick 25, pick 26, and a 2028 third-round pick going back the other way.

Former top-five pick on the move

Zane Duursma has got his wish, joining Melbourne along with pick 52. The Roos get pick 33 and 49 in return.

Blues ruck crosses to Collingwood

Flynn Riley has been traded to the Magpies after joining Carlton in the mid-season draft this year, making his AFL debut in Round 18.

A 2028 third-round pick goes the Blues' way.

Swans trade star defender to North Melbourne

The biggest name left on the AFL trade board has tumbled, with Sydney agreeing to move Nick Blakey to North Melbourne.

The Swans offloaded Blakey, draft pick No.52 and their 2028 second-round selection in exchange for a glut of picks.

The Kangaroos traded picks No.6 and No.47, a 2027 second-round pick, a 2028 first-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to get the deal done.

Monday Oct. 12
Suns land Schubert, Butler from Hawks

The Suns have landed their offseason trade target in Aidan Schubert from Hawthorn, in a package also involving Sam Butler and some picks going both ways.

Gold Coast gained Schubert, Butler, Hawthorn's 2028 first-round pick, and Hawthorn's 2027 third-round pick, in exchange for Gold Coast's 2028 first-rounder, and second rounders in both 2027 and 2028.

Friday, Oct. 9
Butters is a Bulldog

Zak Butters is officially a Western Bulldog. Port Adelaide will not match the offer and accept pick No. 5 as compensation, having also earlier secured picks 6, 10, and two future-firsts in the five-club mega trade. The star free agent and three-time All-Australian, who played 156 games and kicked 73 goals for the Power after being drafted in 2019, has signed a nine-year deal with his boyhood club

Hawks land spearhead King

After securing Zach Merrett earlier this week, Hawthorn have officially welcomed Ben King today after gold Coast elected not to match the offer for the restricted free agent. the Suns will receive a first round pick as compensation, which currently stands at pick No. 7.

Mega trade approved

The league approved a mega trade involving Port Adelaide, the Bulldogs, Melbourne, Hawthorn and Carlton, two players and scores of picks.

Under the five-team deal, the Bulldogs gave up picks No. 12 and No. 31 and a 2028 first-rounder to bring in Hawthorn's Finn Maginness, Carlton's Hudson O'Keeffe and later picks in this year's draft and future years.

Port parted with picks No. 4, 46 and 81 and six second-round or worse future selections to get back picks No. 6 and No. 10, Melbourne's 2027 first-rounder and the Dogs' 2028 first-rounder.

The Demons surrendered picks No.6, 10 and 87 and their 2027 first-rounder -- as well as two late future picks -- for picks No. 4, 12, 31 and 46.

Hawthorn (2027 third-rounder) and Carlton (2028 fourth-rounder) received late future picks for Maginness and O'Keeffe.

-- AAP

Flag Lion gets his wish

Brisbane has traded second-year Lion and 2025 premiership player Sam Marshall and pick No. 39 to St Kilda for a 2027 first-rounder.

Thursday, Oct. 8
Marshall lands at the Cats

St Kilda have pulled the trigger on a deal to send contracted ruckman Rowan Marshall to Geelong, as the Cats and other rival clubs circle Sydney star Nick Blakey.

Geelong traded pick No.14 in this year's draft for the disenchanted 30-year-old and a third-round selection in 2028 on Thursday afternoon.

New Zealand-born Marshall had requested a move to the Cats for a second straight year after St Kilda recruited Tom De Koning to become their first-choice ruckman.

-- AAP

Wednesday, Oct. 7
Dons defender gets traded to the Cats

After being denied a trade last year, Jordan Ridley got his wish for a fresh start after Essendon and Geelong agreed to a deal on Wednesday.

Geelong gave up utility Jack Bowes, a 2027 first-round pick and 2028 second-round pick to get the 27-year-old Ridley through the door.

Pick No. 60 and a 2028 fourth-round selection will come back to the Cats from the Bombers.

--AAP

Tuesday, Oct. 6
O'Driscoll makes the move over east

Fremantle have traded 24-year-old Nathan O'Driscoll to Richmond in exchange for pick 61 in this year's draft.

The winger played 17 games for the Dockers this season but wasn't selected for the Grand Final.

Monday, Oct. 5
TRADE PERIOD OPENS
Merrett finally becomes a Hawk

After attempting to join Hawthorn last year, Zach Merrett has finally been traded from Essendon to the Hawks.

Hawthorn have sent picks 15, 25 and a 2028 second-round pick in exchange for the 31-year-old.

Merrett leaves the Bombers a week after winning a record-equaling seventh Crichton Medal, three All-Australian blazers, and 274 games.

Pendlebury becomes a Sun

AFL games record holder Scott Pendlebury is officially a Sun after Gold Coast and Collingwood agreed on a trade for the 38-year-old veteran.

Pendlebury, a two-time premiership player, heads to the Suns in exchange for pick No. 65 in this year's draft.

"It's an exciting group here at the SUNS and the opportunity to bring a few different ideas and also learn from a great group of coaches and players is one I'm really looking forward to," Pendlebury told the Suns.

"This side is one I've watched from afar and really admired. I've got a bit of knowledge about the industry so I'm here to play my role and help this squad continue to develop."

Jesse Hogan traded from GWS to Collingwood

Out-of-favour Giants forward Jesse Hogan has made the switch to Collingwood in exchange for pick 75.

The 31-year-old won the Coleman Medal in 2024 but has been unable to recapture his best form at the Giants in the two years since.

Magpies list boss Justin Leppitsch said Hogan would be a valuable addition.

"On behalf of everyone at Collingwood, I'd like to warmly welcome Jesse to Collingwood. Jesse has established himself as one of the competition's premier key forwards and we're excited to see him bring his experience and talent to our club," he said.

"His aerial presence inside forward-50 and his consistency as a goal-kicker make him a genuine threat.

"Like Lachie (Neale), Jesse has a passion to teach the next generation and will make a great addition to our club."

Saturday, Oct. 3
Bulldogs seal free-agency signing of key defender

The Western Bulldogs have finally snagged the key defender they need, securing Adelaide backman Jordon Butts as an unrestricted free agent.

The Bulldogs are set for a bumper AFL trade period headlined by working through a deal for Port Adelaide superstar Zak Butters, ahead of a 2027 season where the club will have high expectations.

But after seeing off Carlton's advances to keep hold of defender Buku Khamis, the Bulldogs have filled a major area of need by adding 26-year-old Butts.

Adelaide will receive a second-round compensation selection, currently pick No.33, in this year's draft.

-- AAP

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Three-peat Lion locks in Magpies move

Lachie Neale has sealed his high-profile switch to Collingwood, with Brisbane teasing the dual Brownlow medallist on his way out the door.

The AFL approved Neale signing a three-year deal with the Magpies on Friday afternoon, closing out the first day of free agency.

The 33-year-old ball-winner leaves as an unrestricted free agent after the Lions clinched a third straight flag with their stunning seven-point grand final victory over Fremantle.

-- AAP

Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: WNBA playoffs 2026: The Valkyries' wild path from expansion team to the Finals
stories.summary: Two years ago, the Valkyries didn't exist. Now they're competing for their first title -- here's how they did it.
stories.body:
As a general rule, expansion teams aren't really supposed to be very good right away. Sure, the initial player draft offers a chance to assess the league's potentially undervalued and overlooked players on the off chance of finding a hidden treasure, but from there, contention usually requires a lot of patience: A bunch of losing seasons provide the high draft picks to slowly accumulate talent, with a legitimate chance to contend finally waiting at the end of that long building process.

The Golden State Valkyries apparently missed that memo.

Barely two seasons into their existence, the Valkyries are headed to the WNBA Finals against the Atlanta Dream (Game 1 at 12:30 p.m. Saturday). To get there, they closed out the Las Vegas Aces on the road. This was a matchup that began as a huge mismatch in team pedigree -- the Aces had won three of the past four WNBA titles, while Golden State literally didn't exist two years ago -- if not talent. Instead, it became a changing of the guard, with the league's new contender sweeping aside one of its greatest dynasties.

Exactly how historic are the Valkyries as a recent expansion team? And how have they managed to go from an expansion draft to a Finals appearance in less than two years? Let's dive into five charts that explain Golden State's unprecedented rise.

Going into 2025, it was a bit of a mystery how the Valkyries would end up doing in their first WNBA season. Previously, expansion teams had posted an average winning percentage of .306 with a minus-8.4 net rating (we're not including 1997, the league's first season). If history was any indication, fans could expect Golden State to be one of the league's worst teams out of the gates.

But before Golden State, the league hadn't added a new team since the Atlanta Dream in 2008, meaning a backlog of great players was building up in competition for the same number of total roster spots in the W. (Witness the number of high draft picks who would be waived heading into each season.) Contrary to the historical record, this suggested the Valkyries would be tapping into a vast reservoir of available talent when building the first WNBA expansion squad in nearly two decades.

And that has largely proved to be true. The Valkyries ended up having the second-best first-year winning percentage (.523) of any WNBA club -- trailing only the 1998 Detroit Shock (.567) -- and the best expansion year by both net rating (plus-1.8) and Elo rating (1494). And all they've done since is continued that meteoric rise, to the point that they had the best regular season for a second-year team by all available measures of team quality, and in fact finished with the second-best record in the league -- and best net rating overall -- in 2026.

As a result of their dramatic rise from, well, not having a team at all in 2024 to the league's top net rating in 2026, the Valkyries' odds of winning the WNBA title also have risen dramatically. Going into the season, Golden State looked like a solid pick to return to the playoffs and possibly even win a series (last year's season ended with a 2-0 first-round sweep to the Minnesota Lynx). But contending for the championship seemed like a much taller order -- especially in a crowded field that contained the former champion Aces and Liberty, plus the improved Olivia Miles version of the Lynx, an Indiana Fever team featuring a healthy Caitlin Clark, and the overhauled Dream.

And for the first few months of the season, that seemed about right. The Valkyries were 13-7 through the end of June, one of the better records in the league but still clearly within a five-team logjam below Minnesota and Las Vegas. It seemed as if Golden State were destined to spend all year fighting for razor-thin seeding margins within that group. But since July 1, the Valkyries rattled off a league-best 19-5 record and saw their odds in statistical systems like Elo zoom past those of the presumed-favorite Lynx by the end of the regular season, when the latter hit a late slump. A 5-1 playoff start has only reinforced their status as a serious title threat, and now the early-season underdog Valkyries are statistical favorites to win it all.

If we had to pick a single calling card for the Valkyries' impressive championship bid, it has to be their defense. With a defensive rating of 100.6, they not only led all teams in suppressing opponents' per-possession scoring, but the gap between Golden State and No. 2 Atlanta at 104.5 (3.9 points per 100 possessions) was roughly the same as the gap between Atlanta and No. 7 New York at 108.7 -- or nearly the gap to league average itself, which was 109.1. The Valkyries' difference compared to that league figure (minus-8.5 points per 100) ranked as the sixth-best single-season WNBA defense ever relative to average.

The 2025 Valkyries landed on a number of top-tier defenders through the expansion draft, including Veronica Burton on the perimeter and Temi Fagbenle on the inside, helping Golden State rank fourth on defense right out of the gate under coach Natalie Nakase. But an even more refined version of the team's D came into shape in 2026, with names like Kiah Stokes -- whose block saved the Valkyries in Game 2 against Vegas -- and Gabby Williams joining Burton this season.

The Valkyries' defensive recipe blends a few components. They have one of the better rim protectors in the league in Stokes, which contributes to a league-low 47.8 effective FG% allowed, plus a couple of premier ball hawks in Burton and Williams, which forces opponents into mistakes -- they also ranked No. 2 in turnover rate forced. And opponents don't get many easy transition opportunities against Golden State because the Valkyries play at the league's slowest pace and hardly ever turn the ball over. Nakase was the lead assistant under Becky Hammon for the 2023 Aces when they had one of the best defenses in WNBA history -- and now she's using those lessons to try to dethrone her old team.

Obviously, a team doesn't post the league's best net rating and fight to within a game of the WNBA Finals without star performances, and the Valkyries absolutely got one of those this season from Burton.

The Northwestern alum was originally taken No. 7 by Dallas in the 2022 draft, but the Wings never really gave her much opportunity to earn an expanded role; she started 19 only total games in her first two seasons, averaging a paltry 14.5 minutes over that span before being waived before the 2024 season. After signing with Connecticut midseason, Burton continued to log backup minutes (12.7 MPG) despite improving her scoring efficiency with increased usage.

It wasn't until Burton, left unprotected in the expansion draft, landed with Golden State that she finally found a situation in which she could start -- and she has thrived in the role. Averaging 29.0 MPG as a Valkyrie, Burton has remained one of the league's top defensive guards while also taking a huge step forward as an offensive presence, which earned her Most Improved Player honors in 2025. But the advanced metrics in particular adore Burton for her two-way play; her ability to draw fouls while still taking plenty of 3s; her playmaking (she maintained a 34.5% assist rate with just an 11.9% turnover rate); and her massive on-court impact, which showed up at both ends of the court. Burton finished the season ranked second behind only the MVP A'ja Wilson in both LAKER wins added and win shares.

Burton had help. Led by Williams, who arrived from Seattle as a big-time impact player in her own right, six additional Valkyries beyond Burton had at least 2.5 LAKER wins added; no other team in the league had more than five players crack that barrier, much less if their top star is tossed out. Add in Nakase, the 2025 WNBA Coach of the Year, and the Valkyries are loaded with talent from top to bottom.

As much as we've been extolling the virtues of Burton's game, she hasn't been as effective as usual in the playoffs -- averaging just 9.5 PPG on 35.3% shooting from the field in six games. She has still made her trademark on-court impact; Golden State has a plus-12.4 net rating when she's in the game, 13.3 points per 100 better than when she sits. And in the clutch, she made multiple big shots when Golden State needed her. But her postseason LAKER rating of plus-2.7 points per 100 is markedly down from her mark of plus-7.5 in the regular season.

Luckily for the Valkyries, they've received big performances from some of the other names on the roster -- most notably Williams, who is averaging 22.7 PPG in the playoffs. Another player who has run with an opportunity in Golden State, Williams was always more of a defensive player than a scorer in her previous career stops, but her usage rate this season (29.0%) was a whopping 11.2 points higher than her previous career average, and she's pushing it even higher (to 32.1%) in the playoffs.

Of course, Williams does have a tendency to raise her game in the postseason (where her career scoring average of 14.5 PPG is markedly higher than her 9.3 regular-season figure), but this is taking things to a new level. And the other Valkyries to raise their output significantly in the playoffs are Tiffany Hayes and Cecilia Zandalasini, who both have produced massive LAKER ratings (Hayes is at plus-10.7!) in around 18 minutes per game off the bench.

It should be noted that the Valkyries' run has involved its fair share of gritty wins, surviving Dallas in a win-or-go-home Game 3 to win in the first round, needing some late free throws and a last-second block to take the 2-0 lead over Las Vegas, and then outlasting the Aces in overtime of the semifinals clincher. There's no question Golden State will have another tough assignment taking down Angel Reese and the Dream -- and the league's second-best defense -- to win a title.

But the Valkyries have spent their entire, brief existence defying conventional expectations for expansion teams. Why should the most significant step yet along their improbable path to a championship be any different?

stories.headline: NRL: Spencer Leniu signs with Eels after early Roosters release
stories.summary: Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.

Leniu finished his three-year stint at the Tricolours on a high after a stellar performance in their 19-18 win over Newcastle to secure the 2026 trophy.

The NSW Origin representative added the Roosters' premiership ring to the three he won with Penrith from 2021-2023.

Leniu was granted a release from the final year of his Roosters contract, which will give the club some salary cap reprieve

The hard-hitting forward's Eels contract is reportedly worth more than the $850,000 per year he was making with Easts, where he spent much of his time coming off the bench.

He is expected to play a more active role in blue and gold, leading the line for the Eels' forward pack.

The westward move will see the former Panther reunite with good friend Jarome Luai, but first the pair will both suit up for Toa Samoa at the Rugby League World Cup.

Eels general manager of football Mark O'Neill shared his delight at signing one of the game's "premier enforcers".

"We're thrilled to have Spencer join the Parramatta Eels and become part of what we're building at this club," O'Neill said in a statement.

"He's one of the elite middle forwards in the game and has consistently performed on the biggest stages throughout his career.

The exit of Leniu adds to the exodus of stars from the Roosters premiership lineup.

Angus Crichton and Mark Nawaqanitawase are rugby-bound, Daly Cherry-Evans is joining Hull FC, while Daniel Tupou retired this week after his 307-game career.

Connor Watson, who missed the title decider due to concussion, has signed for a season with St George Illawarra Dragons.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson said Leniu had been a strong contributor during his time at the club.

"Spencer has brought a lot to our group over the last three years, both through the way he plays and the energy and personality he brings every day," Robinson said in a statement on Thursday.

"He brings an intensity and competitiveness to everything he does, and he challenges the people around him to be better.

"To see him finish his time here as a premiership winner is something he should be really proud of, and something we'll always share together."

With his departure announced at the Roosters' awards night on Wednesday, Leniu said he would leave the club on a high.

""I'm proud to have worn the Roosters jersey and I'll always have a lot of love and respect for the club, the boys and everyone who has supported me during my time here," said Leniu.

"Winning a premiership with this group and sharing that with the boys, our families and everyone at the club is something I'll carry with me for the rest of my life."

stories.headline: Galatasaray boosted by Victor Osimhen return for Barcelona clash in UEFA Champions League
stories.summary: Victor Osimhen marked his return from a month-long injury absence with an assist against Kasımpasa, giving the Turkish champions a boost ahead of their UEFA Champions League meeting with Barcelona.
stories.body:
Victor Osimhen marked his return from a month-long injury absence with an assist as 10-man Galatasaray scored twice in stoppage time to defeat Kasımpasa 3-1 on Friday, giving the Turkish champions a boost ahead of their UEFA Champions League meeting with Barcelona.

The Nigeria international came off the bench in the 77th minute and set up Mario Lemina's stoppage-time goal, marking his first competitive appearance since suffering a groin injury Sept. 4.

Osimhen's return provides a timely boost for the Turkish champions ahead of Tuesday's home game against Barcelona, although it remains unclear whether the 27-year-old striker is fit enough to start.

Galatasaray had managed his recovery cautiously, after medical examinations revealed a strain and bleeding in his right adductor muscle group. He resumed partial team training last week before being named among the substitutes against Kasimpasa.

The hosts led through Abdülkerim Bardakçi's first-half goal but were reduced to 10 men when Lucas Torreira was sent off in the 63rd minute. Jesurun Rak-Sakyi equalized five minutes later, leaving Galatasaray facing the prospect of dropping points.

Osimhen replaced Deniz Gül alongside Leroy Sané's introduction in the 77th minute and made an immediate impact, setting up a chance for the German winger before having an effort saved himself.

Baris Alper Yilmaz restored Galatasaray's lead in the 90th minute before Osimhen combined with Lemina for the Gabon international to seal victory six minutes into stoppage time. The win moved Galatasaray provisionally to the top of the Turkish Super Lig with 16 points from seven matches.

Osimhen's return will be welcomed by Galatasaray, who had been without their leading striker during a difficult period that included a league defeat to Trabzonspor and a 3-1 loss to Sporting Lisbon in their Champions League opener.

The Nigerian had scored six goals in four appearances before his season was interrupted by the injury.

His absence also affected Nigeria's preparations for their recent Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, where the Super Eagles struggled to edge a gutsy Madagascar, then suffered defeat to Guinea-Bissau.

Osimhen's return to competitive football will also be welcomed by Nigeria ahead of next month's international window, when Chelle will hope to have his first-choice striker available again for back to back games against Tanzania.

Additionally, the forward can resume his interrupted pursuit of Rashidi Yekini's national-team scoring record, with just two goals needed to equal the record, and three to go ahead of the legendary striker.

stories.headline: Source: Dodgers' decision on sitting Ohtani hinges on health
stories.summary: The Dodgers will gauge whether Shohei Ohtani's lingering injuries warrant him sitting out but will keep playing him if he deems himself healthy, a source said.
stories.body:
MILWAUKEE -- The Los Angeles Dodgers plan to gauge whether superstar Shohei Ohtani's lingering injuries warrant him sitting out Game 3 of the National League Championship Series but will continue playing him if he deems himself healthy, a source told ESPN.

Ohtani went 0-for-4 with two strikeouts in a 7-4 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 2 on Monday that put the Dodgers in a 2-0 hole in the best-of-seven series. Afterward, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told The Athletic he would have "a conversation" with Ohtani during Tuesday's workout in L.A. to "try to figure out what's best for him."

But a source clarified that the team would sit Ohtani only if he believed he was compromised by the left knee and right bicep injuries that previously hindered him. If he feels good enough to play, the plan is to continue playing him.

Ohtani has not homered since Aug. 18 and has produced only three hits in 20 postseason at-bats. Over the past eight weeks, a stretch in which he went on the injured list in hopes of helping his body recover, he is slashing .156/.283/.200.

"It's hard to see," Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts said of Ohtani's struggles. "He's working, and hopefully he gets out of it. We know he's working. Yeah, that's a big one. We need him for sure."

When Betts grounded out for the first out of the fifth inning Monday, he pumped his fist in celebration. To him, it meant something more -- that Tommy Edman would move to third base, allowing him to later score the go-ahead run on a sacrifice fly, and that perhaps the Dodgers had finally tapped into something against this vaunted Brewers pitching staff.

Betts' zeal, it turns out, was fleeting.

For the second time in as many games in this NLCS, the Dodgers were shut down by a dominant bullpen in the later innings, unable to match a relentless Brewers offense that continuously applied pressure. Rather than set the tone, Betts' groundout represented the first of 15 consecutive outs recorded by Brewers relievers, a sign that the Dodgers' struggles extend well beyond Ohtani.

Thirty-six of the past 38 teams that faced a 2-0 deficit in a best-of-seven series were ultimately eliminated. To Freddie Freeman and so many of his teammates, the reason the Dodgers are in this position is quite simple.

"They got on base and got the hits," Freeman said. "It's hard to win games when you only get three hits."

Once again, none of those hits came with runners in scoring position. The Dodgers went 0-for-4 in that situation in Game 2 and are now 2-for-26 with runners in scoring position in these playoffs, with both of those hits coming off the bat of Andy Pages. Of the 19 runs the Dodgers have scored in their first six games this month, 11 have come via home run.

The struggles are collective, but none feel bigger than the ones endured by Ohtani.

The most glaring sign of his struggles occurred in Monday's sixth inning, when he squared to bunt to begin his at-bat. Five JoJo Romero pitches later, he struck out while awkwardly chasing a sweeper well out of the zone.

"It's tough," Dodgers outfielder Teoscar Hernandez said. "We obviously need his help. He's a big, big part of this team, and it's really important. And just like, you know, I feel bad for him. I know what he's capable of. He's been dealing with some stuff in the past. We don't know if it's still there. But it's Shohei. Any moment, he can come through."

Yoshinobu Yamamoto, arguably the best postseason pitcher going right now, was removed after recording only eight outs and throwing 75 pitches -- 12 of them in one encounter with Jake Bauers, who drew a third-inning walk to load the bases and set up Christian Yelich's two-run single, forcing Roberts to go to his bullpen earlier than he had hoped.

If Will Smith challenges two borderline two-strike pitches to Brice Turang in the first and third innings, both of which ultimately led to runs, maybe Yamamoto's outing looks different. If Roberts brings Roki Sasaki back out for the fifth inning -- rather than turning to lefty Kris Bubic, who proceeded to give up the William Contreras home run that tied the score at 4 -- maybe the Brewers don't gain momentum. And if Brock Stewart doesn't make an errant pickoff throw to first base in the bottom of the sixth, allowing David Hamilton to later score on Contreras' single, maybe everything is different.

But the reality is this: The Dodgers' offense has produced almost nothing late.

In Game 1, they stressed Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski enough to force him out in the fifth inning. In Game 2, they did the same to rookie Logan Henderson, who was removed after his second throwing error. But in both, six relievers -- a group headlined by Aaron Ashby, Abner Uribe and Trevor Megill -- combined to allow only five of 33 batters to reach to reach base.

The last time the Dodgers dropped the first two games in a playoff series, it was 2023. They were swept out of the NL Division Series by a red-hot Arizona Diamondbacks team then. Immediately after that, they signed Ohtani, surrounded him with a host of high-priced stars and won the next two championships.

Now the question is whether Ohtani will be there to help them get out of this hole.

"We're all still behind him," Dodgers third baseman Max Muncy said. "He knows we're all still behind him. He's going to get a big hit for us. I know that. I can tell you right now he's going to get a big hit for us at some point, and that's going to turn things."

stories.headline: Premier League overreactions: Takeaways from first games post-international break
stories.summary: After a three-week intermission, the Premier League returned with a bang last weekend. Will Man City eventually crumble under the pressure? Is this the real Man United? Let's overreact!
stories.body:
It was another wild weekend of Premier League action. Manchester City took their first steps on the field after they were charged by the Premier League, but they showed signs of being distracted by that as they put in a statement performance against Liverpool.

Elsewhere, we saw Brighton & Hove Albion win again, Manchester United stutter at home to Tottenham Hotspur, Fulham slump to yet another defeat and Florian Wirtz continue to struggle.

There are plenty of takes around after the weekend, and ahead of the next batch of fixtures -- like we've done with NFL and rugby union -- we look at some snap judgements before weighing up whether they are overreactions or legit takes.

Let's start with the match at Anfield.

Jump to:

Man City will crumble under opposing fans' anger?

Wirtz's poor form a huge concern for Liverpool?

United's past success under Carrick a mirage?

Brighton will make Champions League?

Fulham's Arbeloa will be first coach sacked?

Man City will eventually be thrown off by the boos

Coach Enzo Maresca said after City's 3-0 win at Anfield that his side must embrace the noise as the league's villains, having been found guilty of 114 out of 115 Premier League charges relating to financial breaches. But Elliot Anderson and other players conceded that adjusting to the intimidating atmosphere was hard in the first half.

The anger across the league is at such a level that wherever City go, opposition fans are going to hammer them. It will eventually prove to be too much for them.

Verdict: OVERREACTION

Before the start of the match at Anfield, amid a cacophony of boos, the City players went over to acknowledge their fans. They were waving inflatable bananas -- a nod to their club's lower-league past -- and gave their players a huge welcome. As Erling Haaland turned away to re-focus on the pitch, the camera caught him smirking. He was in his element.

Post-match, the players admitted that the venom levelled at them threw them off their stride. But after Ryan Gravenberch's red card on the 62nd minute, they found their tempo and took control of the match. It was a masterclass in mental vigor.

This noise isn't going to go away. If anything, as City continue racking up win after win, it's going to get even more ferocious.

But judging by Sunday, they are going to feed off it. At home, the Etihad Stadium atmosphere will be more vocal than ever before. On the road, if Haaland's role of embracing the villain is anything to go by, they are clearly trying to channel the vitriol as fuel.

All the while, we wait for the result of City's appeal and any subsequent sanctions. The sight of City's players celebrating the 3-0 win is going to fire up the rest of the league even more, but the signs so far are they have the mental fortitude to cope with this.

Liverpool should be concerned about Wirtz's form

When Bayer Leverkusen won the Bundesliga, Wirtz was the heartbeat of the side. At Liverpool, things have not gone nearly as smoothly for him.

The match against City was another opportunity for Wirtz to kick-start his season -- and his Liverpool career -- but it passed him by. It's not for want of trying, but in his 39 Premier League matches since joining in June 2025, he has contributed five goals and five assists. That's not form worthy of the £116 million Liverpool spent to sign him.

Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION

It's just not clicking for the incredibly gifted forward at Anfield. It's befuddling -- Wirtz should work in the Premier League. He's technically brilliant, he's positionally astute and he has the vision to unpick defenses. But for whatever reason, he has not looked like the same player he was with Leverkusen.

His work off the ball is also winning few admirers. Pundit and former Liverpool player Jamie Carragher summed it all up perfectly on Sky Sports after the City game: "He shouldn't be in the Liverpool team right now. I don't want to hammer Liverpool players. But we're not saying this after five to 10 games; we're saying this after 50 to 60 games.

"Wirtz never looks like scoring a goal. You don't come away thinking he missed chances or he worked the goalkeeper. There was absolutely nothing today where you thought he put someone through or nearly scored."

The issue is, if Liverpool were to cut ties with Wirtz -- Bayern Munich have been long-term admirers, and just about any team in the Bundesliga would take him -- they'd have to stomach a hefty loss.

Jurgen Klopp remains a believer with Germany, and Wirtz could still come good at Liverpool. I personally hope he does: I still remember the player I watched at Leverkusen and the excitement whenever he got the ball. He will be given more time, but the clock is ticking.

Last season's success under Carrick was a mirage -- this is the real Man United

That familiar feeling of unrest and fading optimism is back at Old Trafford. On Saturday, Manchester United failed to get past Spurs, who managed to scramble an equalizer in the 92nd minute despite being reduced to 10 men when Rodrigo Bentancur was sent off in the 78th minute.

The pressure is mounting on coach Michael Carrick. Last season's third-place finish seems a world away and from a different life: this is the real United we're seeing now.

Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION

The case of midfielder Andrey Santos is baffling. A £50 million signing from Chelsea, he has started just one of their six Premier League matches to date. That was their opener against Hull City -- and in their past three games, he has remained on the bench. How Carrick must wish that money had been spent elsewhere: on the left back they've been crying out for, or on an experienced striker to offer another option up front.

Santos' situation is symptomatic of the wider malaise at United. The match against Spurs offered them the perfect chance to kick-start their season: Spurs are without a win and also facing mounting pressure. But instead, United were outplayed for much of the match.

United have been on the wrong side of some small margins this term, and perhaps they are on the verge of springing into life, but the results are telling a different story. The summer featured pointed recruitment on midfield, but that has left Carrick shortchanged in key areas.

Their next three league matches are tricky: Leeds United away, AFC Bournemouth at home and Chelsea away on Oct. 31. They also have two UEFA Champions League trips during that batch.

Fans are waiting for the real United to stand up. The concern is last season was a blissful mirage, and this is the real thing as United's fans endure another false dawn.

Brighton will qualify for the Champions League

Brighton & Hove Albion have their best squad in years, and have already knocked over Aston Villa and Arsenal this season. Down to 10 men for the final 33 minutes against Sunderland on Saturday, they still came away with the 2-0 win at the Stadium of Light. There's no reason why they can't qualify for the Champions League this term.

Verdict: OVERREACTION

There used to be a sign on the walls of Brighton's offices at the American Express Stadium that outlined the club's goal: "To be a top-10 club in the Premier League and a top four club in the WSL." That was their aim back in the 2022-23 season, the days of Roberto de Zerbi, Alexis Mac Allister and Moisés Caicedo.

Four years later, Brighton's league finishes since then have been sixth, 11th, eighth and eighth. The sign is gone. The club has higher aspirations.

There were some nerves in and around the club over the summer when last season's top scorer Danny Welbeck left and James Milner retired. That was a lot of the club's experience walking out the door. But Brighton always have a plan, and so far this season, they've taken another step.

Back on Sept. 19, they were irresistible in a big win against Arsenal. They have everyone is singing off the same hymn sheet, comfortable with the club's aims and steered towards their collective goal. After six matches, they sit in fifth. They can keep this run going.

There's not much point planning a new sign with the club's next target, as they'll probably kick past that before they have a chance to get the sign on the wall. With the Premier League likely to get five Champions League spots, Brighton can absolutely grab one of them.

Arbeloa is the front-runner in the the Premier League's "sack race"

Fulham remain without a win and anchored to the foot of the Premier League. Saturday's match against Ipswich Town was the perfect opportunity to get the season off and running. It looked like they were going to do just that as the match reached its closing stages: Ryan Sessegnon's goal had given Fulham the lead. But then Abdoul Ouattara equalized, and four minutes later, Dara O'Shea scored the winner.

Six matches into his reign, Arbeloa's job is hanging by a thread.

Verdict: NOT AN OVERREACTION

There are signs that Fulham's league position is an unfair reflection of how well they're playing. Their expected-goals (xG) total of 9.56 ranks eighth in the league; their actual return of six goals from their six matches is far below what they should have managed. The issue is, Fulham's self-belief is creaking, and their record of conceding late goals is a problem.

Arbeloa was defiant after the Ipswich match, but the pressure is increasing. "I am a coach so I never worry about my position," Arbeloa said afterward. "I don't feel fear. You cannot be a coach if you feel it."

Gary O'Neil, Ipswich's manager, felt Fulham tired in the closing stages of the match. Despite some signs Fulham are on the cusp of exploding into life, the win they need evades them.

There are pockets of Fulham's support who have already had enough of Arbeloa. Take this headline from Fulham-focused publication "Saturday White Fever": "Arbeloa must go now -- it's time for the Khans to axe incompetent Spaniard and avoid sleepwalking to their fourth relegation."

Arbeloa needs wins, and quickly. The match on Saturday against Hull is huge.

stories.headline: Rams' Alaric Jackson punches Bills' Bradley Chubb after MNF
stories.summary: On the field after the Los Angeles Rams' 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night, Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson punched Bills outside linebacker Bradley Chubb in a scene captured by ESPN's cameras at SoFi Stadium.
stories.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- On the field after the Los Angeles Rams' 37-34 overtime loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday night, Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson punched Bills outside linebacker Bradley Chubb.

In a scene captured by ESPN's cameras, Jackson stood near midfield after the game while exchanging jerseys with Bills defensive lineman Deone Walker when it appeared Chubb said something to Jackson. Jackson then walked toward Chubb before punching him in the face with his right hand.

"It's just emotions, you know what I mean? Emotional game. It was a close game," Chubb told the California Post in Buffalo's locker room. "And, you know, they always catch the second guy. So, I let him swing. And then my teammates held me back, and I just chilled."

Jackson was pulled away by Rams tight end Colby Parkinson after the punch.

"Like I said, it was emotional game. Tempers got flared," Chubb said. "But it is what it is. We flushed it and we onto next week."

Chubb was still in full uniform at the time, while Jackson had removed his shoulder pads and jersey before walking up to Chubb.

"Somebody swung, but hey, that's not on me to tell who," Chubb said. "There's cameras out there. I just know, you know what I'm saying, I'm just ready for next week."

When asked if the punch connected, Chubb responded, "I'm just ready for next week. ... You see, I'm smiling, I'm with my team. ... I'll be ready for next week."

Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson weighed in on social media, writing on X, "So what we gone do about dude hitting Chub!"

Apart from Chubb and Gardner-Johnson's post, neither team addressed the incident.

The Bills will take on the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, and the Rams host the Arizona Cardinals.

stories.headline: Toto Wolff finds quirky solution to Kimi Antonelli track limits 'stress'
stories.summary: Toto Wolff joked he would shove a pillow under the a--e of Kimi Antonelli before hailing the Italian's maturity as he moved within reach of the world championship.
stories.body:
Toto Wolff joked he would shove a pillow under the a--e of Kimi Antonelli before hailing the Italian's maturity as he moved within reach of the world championship.

Antonelli claimed third place under the lights in Singapore on Sunday to stretch his advantage in the drivers' standings to 102 points ahead of Mercedes teammate George Russell.

That opens the possibility that the 20-year-old could confirm his place as Formula 1's youngest world champion at the next round in Texas in a fortnight. As things stand, he would need to win at the Circuit of the Americas with Russell ninth or lower and Lewis Hamilton fifth or lower.

Antonelli's dominance of the season has been remarkable, especially given his difficult debut campaign last year, and he is all-but certain to clinch his place in the sport's history books over the next few races.

He has, though, proved that he has a penchant for pushing track limits. He again received a final warning for the violation in Singapore, as he has done on several occasions this season, with one more fault leading to a penalty.

Mercedes boss Wolff has a solution as he admitted it causes tension on the pit wall.

"I have a good strategy, I'm going to put a pillow from the hotel under his a--e, under his butt, so he can actually see the road," Wolff said.

"Because I think it's like this, you know, he can't see it [the track].

"So yeah, under his a--e so he can see, and it stresses us. Half the race we already have three strikes, but it also shows that he's pushing the limits a lot."

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

- Red Bull downplay 'team to beat' label by George Russell, Oscar Piastri

- Lando Norris takes responsibility for collision with Oscar Piastri in Singapore: 'I let McLaren down'

Antonelli was off the pace for much of the weekend in Singapore but profited from the McLaren pair colliding to take fourth in Saturday's sprint before making late moves to rise from fifth to third in Sunday's main event.

Max Verstappen completed a perfect weekend, backing up sprint victory with a dominant race. The four-time world champion remains 119 points adrift, with Antonelli admitting it would be "very scary" if the Dutchman were in the title fight.

Antonelli was on the radio during the race to ask about issues he felt with the car but battled on to ultimately stand on the podium. Russell recovered to ninth after having to start from the back of the grid.

"I think how he [Antonelli] has driven is mature and good," Wolff added. "We talked about it and he said, 'I've just got to keep my calm here and make sure that I finish the race.'

"So handling a difficult car at that stage and trying to develop it and learn, it's good."

It remains a possibility that the penultimate round in Qatar could be cancelled and the season finale in Abu Dhabi replaced by Imola -- if F1 bosses decide they cannot race in the Middle East due to the ongoing conflict.

If that happened, 25 available points would be off the table, moving the Italian ever closer to the championship.

"I haven't looked at it from that perspective because at the moment I have the thought of how many points is it actually and when could he win it?" Wolff said.

"The aim must be to score points, not to lose too many on the others.

"And then it's going to come towards him. And whether that's in Mexico or Brazil or further down the line, we shall see.

"And I guess whether Qatar and Abu Dhabi happens at the moment, everybody says so. You need to go the direction of this is six more races to go and not four."
